11583.take: Opening the window is the first step, but he'll likely need several full practices and won't be a factor until Week 10 or later. Even then he projects as a change-of-pace back behind Hubbard, so his redraft value is a deep stash at best. In dynasty, he's young and was a high pick, but a torn ACL and now core surgery have cut into his outlook; a rebuilding team can buy him cheaply as a lottery ticket. Don't pay much.

13302.name: Adam Randall
13302.headline: Neck injury healed; rookie RB set to come off IR
13302.news: Baltimore placed the rookie running back on injured reserve with a designation to return on Aug. 30, before cutdown day. Later reports said the injury was to his neck. He has now been designated to return and was a full participant in practice this week ahead of Thursday's Nov. 5 game against Jacksonville. As of Wednesday morning we had not seen a confirmed activation to the 53-man roster. A StackedFantasy feed listed him as still on IR as of Oct. 30. He has not played an NFL regular-season snap.
13302.take: Full practices are a good sign, but he is coming back on a short week into an offense with a third-string undrafted rookie at quarterback, so his early role is likely small. He would be behind the established backfield and would only matter right away if the lead back gets hurt. In 12-team redraft he is not a roster add yet. For a rebuilding dynasty team he is a cheap young back worth a stash. Watch his snaps over the next two to three games before spending real assets on him.

11625.name: Adonai Mitchell
11625.headline: Reported 7-142-1 breakout; Jets' downfield role is his
11625.news: Mitchell broke out in the Jets' Nov. 1 game with a reported 7 catches for 142 yards and a touchdown. He drew a 28.1% target share and ran about 80% of routes. We could not find a box score in our searches to confirm the line independently. This came a week after his Week 7 return from a four-game absence with a finger injury, when he did not catch any of his three targets against Miami. Garrett Wilson remains New York's WR1, and Mitchell is the downfield option opposite him.
11625.take: An 80% route rate and a 28% target share are starter usage, not a fluke snap count, which is what makes the game meaningful. The Jets' passing volume and his up-and-down history (0 catches the week before) mean he is a boom-or-bust WR3/flex in 12-team redraft, not a locked-in starter. In dynasty he is young and the role is real, so a rebuilding team should hold him. If someone treats one big game as a reason to pay a premium, listen, but don't sell cheap.

13296.name: Caleb Douglas
13296.headline: Tied for team-high six targets; waiver option again
13296.news: Douglas tied for Miami's team lead with six targets in the 24-19 loss to New England on Nov. 1. We could not verify his catches and yardage from that game. A week earlier, in his first game back from IR after an ankle injury, he caught 2 passes for 70 yards and two touchdowns on three targets against the Jets. He was viewed as Miami's WR1 early in the season before the injury, and several outlets list him as a Week 9 waiver option.
13296.take: Going from three targets to a share of the team lead is the right direction, and it suggests the touchdowns in Week 7 weren't just luck. Miami's passing game spreads the ball around, so expect week-to-week swings. In 12-team redraft he's a reasonable bench add and a deep-league flex. In dynasty, a rookie who was the No. 1 receiver before getting hurt is a cheap buy for a rebuilding team.

13402.name: Skyler Bell
13402.headline: Palmer hamstring could reopen snaps for rookie Bell
13402.news: Bills receiver Joshua Palmer left Buffalo's Week 8 win over Baltimore on Nov. 1 with a hamstring injury and was listed as doubtful to return. Bell, a rookie, was a healthy scratch in that game and is now off the injury report. He missed most of August with a groin injury. His NFL debut came in Week 5 against the Rams while Palmer was out, and one report said he played 61% of the snaps after being inactive for the first four weeks. No Week 9 role has been announced.
13402.take: Bell's playing time has depended on Palmer being out, and that may happen again. Even so, his history of being a healthy scratch in a deep receiver room means we need to see snaps before trusting him. In 12-team redraft, he's only a waiver watch until Palmer's status is clear. In dynasty, he's a cheap rookie with some real chance of playing time, a fine low-cost buy for a rebuilding team.
